---
title: "Versioning Docs"
---

Each version is one rendered site, kept in its own directory. The latest
render is also copied to `/`. Older directories stay as they were.

```text
/                         current release
/v0.3/                    render of tag v0.3.0
/v0.2/                    render of tag v0.2.0
/askr-versions.json       the only version list
```

`/askr-versions.json`:

```json
{
  "mode": "inline",
  "versions": [
    {"label": "0.3", "root": "/", "latest": true},
    {"label": "0.2", "root": "/v0.2/"}
  ]
}
```

`inline` prints the version on a short title, as in `Askr  0.3`. `title` is
for a long name: the header shows the name and a chevron, and the version
number appears only in the menu. This gallery's long-name specimen is
[Versioning Docs with a long title](/usage/versions.html?askr-version-mode=title).

Publishing a new release:

1. Render the tag you are freezing.
2. Put that `_site` in `/v0.4/`.
3. Copy the same files to `/`.
4. Add `0.4` to `/askr-versions.json`.

Leave `/v0.2/` and `/v0.3/` untouched. Their pages, Page Lists, and Areas stay
the text of that tag.

The menu keeps the current path. From `/v0.3/reference/api.html`, choosing 0.2
opens `/v0.2/reference/api.html`.

Askr does not invent that missing page. The project adds a `404.qmd`. When the
path contains a version directory, the page sends the reader to that version's
home. This still works when the site is published under a repository prefix
such as `/askr/`:

```html
<script>
var path = location.pathname;
var version = path.match(/(\/v[^/]+)\//);
if (version) location.replace(path.slice(0, version.index) + version[1] + "/");
</script>
```

This gallery has that page. Version 0.2 is only [its home](/v0.2/). Open this
Versioning Docs page, then choose 0.2: that page is not in 0.2, so you land on
the 0.2 home. `longTitle` in this gallery's JSON is only for the long-name
specimen above. A project omits it.
